summary.headline: Gujarat Energy Q1 FY27 revenue rose 63% to INR9,670 crores and PAT 78% to INR998 crores, led by gas trading EBT of INR726 crores.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR9,670 crores (up 63% YoY), EBITDA INR1,482 crores (up 65%) and PAT INR998 crores (up 78%), with total sales volume of 15.66 mmscmd. Gas trading EBT rose 206% to INR726 crores, helped by Brent-linked long-term contracts and a Morbi industrial volume surge during the Middle East-driven propane shortage. Management kept FY27 gas trading profit guidance at about INR1,100 crores (reiterated as INR1,100-1,200 crores in one answer) and CGD EBITDA guidance at INR5.5-6.5/scm, while saying Morbi volumes will likely settle near 3 mmscmd as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources.

segments.name: Gas trading
segments.commentary: Sales volume 12.22 mmscmd, of which 8.9 mmscmd was transferred to CGD and about 3.3 mmscmd was external; EBT INR726 crores. Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd earlier, due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and lower power volumes; long-term third-party volume expected at 4.5-5 mmscmd in FY28-29.

segments.name: CGD - CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.76 mmscmd, up 13% from 3.33 mmscmd (Gujarat +12%, outside Gujarat +19%). Network at 844 stations after adding 6 and upgrading 9 in the quarter; plans for more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades in FY27.

segments.name: CGD - PNG domestic
segments.commentary: Added about 59,000 domestic PNG customers in the quarter, taking the base above 2.477 million households. Commercial PNG volume was 0.17 mmscmd with more than 16,600 commercial customers.

segments.name: PNG industrial
segments.commentary: Volume 7.17 mmscmd vs 4.71 mmscmd, up 64%. Morbi averaged 5.67 mmscmd and non-Morbi 2.04 mmscmd; non-Morbi realisation about INR70/scm and Morbi about INR78/scm, against propane at about INR65/scm.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Gas-based plants run at very low utilisation: about 6% PLF at the 51 MW GSEG plant and about 1% at Pipavav in Q1, with peak summer demand the only driver.

segments.name: E&P and renewables
segments.commentary: Q1 FY26 EBITDA was INR7 crores (E&P) and INR14 crores (renewables); Q4 FY26 was INR14 crores and INR5 crores. No Q1 FY27 figures were given on the call.

guidance_outlook: Gas trading profit guidance kept at about INR1,100 crores for FY27 on total trading volume, with a 4-5% margin target; one answer cited INR1,100-1,200 crores.
CGD EBITDA guidance kept at INR5.5-6.5/scm; Q2 FY27 is the earliest point for firmer FY27 numbers given Middle East volatility.
CGD capex guided at about INR1,000 crores; no capex planned for gas trading; propane import terminal capex excluded and at early study stage, with capex over the next two years.
Morbi gas volume expected at about 3 mmscmd near term; 1.8-2 mmscmd assumed as a floor on one-month contracts.
Non-Morbi industrial volume targeted at 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise.
Long-term sourcing about 28% (about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent) today, targeted at least 4 million tonnes by 2030; new long-term supply from 2028.
Concrete plan for deploying about INR7,200 crores cash expected by Q3 FY27.
GSPL Transmission listing expected towards early September 2026; Q2 results around mid-November.
capex_capacity: CGD capex of about INR1,000 crores guided for FY27; INR127 crores invested in CGD infrastructure in Q1.
CNG network at 844 stations; more than 75 new stations and about 70 upgrades planned in FY27.
Pipeline network about 45,900 km across six states and one union territory.
Own propane import and storage terminal near Morbi: sites shortlisted in Gujarat, detailed project report pending, capex over about two years and not in the INR1,000 crore plan.
Gas sourcing for CGD: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term, and about 69% short-term or inter-segment.
demand_pricing: Morbi current run-rate about 3 mmscmd of gas vs about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from the US and Venezuela after July.
Management said spot prices near $20/mmBtu make gas costlier than propane, so volume recovery is unlikely near term.
Gas trading sourcing: about 20% long-term (Brent-linked, of which about 20% Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic, about 67% spot.
Gas trading margin: fertilizer marketing margin is fixed at about INR20/scm; industrial margins are market-driven. Management said there will be no negative trading quarters.
Morbi volume rose from about 0.4 mmscmd in April 2026 to about 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the Morbi cluster up 181% vs Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How do 15.66 mmscmd total volume, 12.2 mmscmd gas trading and 12.34 mmscmd CGD reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15.66 is the company total and CGD is 12.34; after removing the 8.9 mmscmd intercompany sale to CGD, external sales are about 3.32 mmscmd.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current Morbi run-rate and how does pricing compare with propane?
qa_highlights.answer: Current Morbi run-rate is about 3 mmscmd of gas versus about 5.3-5.4 mmscmd equivalent of propane, as propane supply recovers from non-Middle East sources. Gas is priced about INR78/scm against propane at about INR65/scm.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG growth outlook for the rest of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects CNG growth of about 12-13% to be sustained for the next couple of years, supported by more than 75 new stations planned in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will third-party gas trading volumes recover, and what is the long-term range?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party volumes fell from about 5 mmscmd to about 3.3 mmscmd due to Middle East supply cuts, high prices and weak power volumes. Management expects long-term third-party volume of 4.5-5 mmscmd, mainly in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sourcing breakup for CGD and gas trading, and what is the long-term share?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD sourcing: about 14% APM, 6% new well gas, 2% GAIL pool, 9% long-term and about 69% short-term or inter-segment. Gas trading: about 20% long-term (about 20% of which is Henry Hub), 12.5% domestic and about 67% spot. Long-term share is about 28%, or about 2 million tonnes LNG equivalent, targeted at 4 million tonnes or more by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gas trading margin high in Q1, and can it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin to timely sourcing and Brent-linked long-term contracts. It ruled out negative trading quarters and maintained FY27 gas trading profit guidance of about INR1,100 crores on total volume, with a 4-5% margin target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CGD EBITDA position against guidance, and why is it below range?
qa_highlights.answer: CGD EBITDA was about INR5.18/scm, below the INR5.5-6.5/scm guidance, which management attributed to a larger volume base. Management kept the guidance and said it looks at portfolio margins rather than segment-level Morbi margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Morbi industrial volume plans and constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Morbi volume is about 2-2.2 mmscmd; management targets at least 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as LNG prices stabilise. It cited infrastructure build-out, with about 86 new industries added in April-June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Morbi volume floor and how is the propane terminal funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumed 1.8-2 mmscmd as a floor on one-month contracts. The propane import terminal is at the site-shortlisting stage, excluded from the INR1,000 crore CGD capex, and would take about two years to build after a detailed project report.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR7,200 crore cash and dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is about INR7,200 crores, with a concrete deployment plan by Q3 FY27 covering CNG, pipelines and energy diversification. It cited dividends of about INR835 crores under Government of Gujarat guidelines.

risks_watch: Morbi volume sustainability: run-rate about 3 mmscmd versus 8 mmscmd in May-June, with the 1.8-2 mmscmd floor on one-month contracts and propane supply recovering.

Gas trading margin durability: Q1 gas trading EBT of INR726 crores against FY27 guidance of about INR1,100 crores, with management stating it is conservative; Q2 visibility limited by Middle East volatility.
CGD EBITDA below guidance at INR5.18/scm against the INR5.5-6.5/scm range; management kept guidance but gave no segment-level explanation.
Third-party gas trading volumes down to about 3.3 mmscmd from about 5 mmscmd, with recovery expected only in FY28-29.
Power segment utilisation very low (about 6% PLF at GSEG and 1% at Pipavav); revival strategy to be shared in a few months.

Pending items: GSPL Transmission listing expected early September 2026, the INR900-odd crore tax refund needing at least a year, and the intercompany transfer-pricing markup between gas trading and CGD.
key_quotes: The Gas Trading segment delivered strong profitability with earnings before tax increasing to INR726 crores in this quarter as against INR237 crores in the previous year same quarter, reflecting a growth of 206%.
Our focus remains clear to maintain the right balance between volume growth and sustainable margins while continuing to serve our customers reliably and efficiently.
No, there will not be any negative numbers. I think we stick to our guidance last time we gave around INR1,100 crores of profit from the gas trading business.
We expect this towards early September.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q1 delivery and the gas trading outlook, but cautious on forward numbers, repeatedly deferring firmer FY27 figures to Q2 because of Middle East volatility. Evasive on segment margin detail, pointing analysts to the investor presentation and declining to break out per-segment CGD margins.

growth.why: Management held FY27 guidance (gas trading profit ~INR1,100-1,200 crore, CGD capex ~INR1,000 crore, CGD EBITDA INR5.5-6.5/scm) but guided Morbi volume down to about 3 mmscmd and third-party volume to 3.3 mmscmd from about 5 mmscmd, and Q1 CGD EBITDA was INR5.18/scm, below range, so the outlook is flat rather than growth.
